finding.title: Flag docs/planning/sync-architecture-plan.md Part A as stale — its outbox-drain headline finding is now false

evidence.quote: grep for `\.drain(` in `lib/` returns zero matches outside `outbox_processor.dart` itself ... The outbox is a write-only sink in production.

finding.why: Running the same grep today finds production callers at lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:384 and lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:200, consistent with the doc's own Phase-0 'Stop the bleeding' rollout item having shipped. The doc reads as a present-tense 'Current-state audit' with no date-of-validity caveat and is unlinked from docs/index.md, so a future contributor or AI agent (this repo runs many 'paste this prompt into a fresh session' orchestration flows) finding it via search could conclude a CRITICAL data-loss bug is still open in the most sync-sensitive subsystem in the app and misdirect effort.
finding.recommendation: Add a 'Part A verified current as of <date>' note, or append a resolved/open marker per ranked finding — mirroring the remediation-status table pattern already used well in tracks-and-completion-bug-report.md.
acceptance_criteria: The doc states the date through which Part A's grep-based claims were last verified, or each of the 15 ranked findings carries a resolved/open marker.

finding.title: Strip leaked `</content>`/`</invoke>` tool-call artifacts from committed planning docs
finding.why: Both files end with literal leftover XML-ish tags from whatever agent tool call authored them (an unstripped Write/Edit tool-call content boundary), not markdown content — verified via direct `tail`/`grep` on disk, independent of any tool rendering. Harmless to rendering but signals the authoring pipeline occasionally commits raw tool-call framing into tracked docs.
finding.recommendation: Delete the trailing artifact lines; add a pre-commit/`make audit` grep for `^</(content|invoke)>$` under docs/ to catch this class of leak before commit (Rule 0 style).
acceptance_criteria: A committed check greps docs/ for stray tool-tag artifacts.

finding.title: Fix wrong bundled seed-asset filename (seed.db.gz) in docs/qa/legacy/14-sync-and-offline.md
finding.rule: Tier-4 triage AREA NOTE — factual-drift check against reality for a presents-as-current doc

evidence.quote: 6. Content DB seed file (`seed.db.gz`) is available in the APK assets
**Preconditions:** Fresh install of the app. The APK contains `seed.db.gz` in assets.

finding.why: A tester following SYNC-29 to verify the seed DB ships in the APK would run `unzip -l app-release.apk | grep seed.db.gz`, find nothing (the real bundled asset is content.db.gz — seed.db.gz is only a local build-only intermediate per tool/seed_content_db.dart), and could file a false 'seed file missing from APK' bug, burning triage time on a doc typo instead of a real defect.
finding.recommendation: Replace both `seed.db.gz` mentions with `content.db.gz`, or add a one-line caveat that seed.db.gz is the pre-bundle build intermediate, never the shipped asset name — matching the correct usage already in the sibling seed-content-db-build-guide.md.
acceptance_criteria: Both occurrences of `seed.db.gz` in docs/qa/legacy/14-sync-and-offline.md (Prerequisites list and SYNC-29) read `content.db.gz` or are annotated as the build-only intermediate name.
grep -c 'seed.db.gz' docs/qa/legacy/14-sync-and-offline.md returns 0, or only appears inside an explicit build-intermediate caveat.
